2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule Nisi, in short, are that the respondent No. 3 as first party filed Labour Case No. 68 of 2016 before the Labour Court for declaration that order of dismissal being office Memo No. 24,04.4745,948.03.014.17.76/2124 dated 10-7-2017 is illegal, void and hence liable to be set-aside and for direction to reinstate him with all arrear wages and service benefits, stating infer altar that he was appointed on 1-4-1995 as permanent helper and his last post was as helper, Srama Daptor (Office) No. 1370, Mota Tat Division, Shift "Ka", Mill No. 1. His service record was satisfactory. The 2nd party-petitioner never suffered any financial loss due to the work of 1st party-respondent No.3. Since the 1st party is an educated person, the 2nd party also engaged him in clerical job but no financial benefit given to the 1st party. The 1st party-respondent No. 3 went on 10 days leave from 6-5-2017 to 15-5-2017 as yearly holiday. Before expiry of 10 days 1st party fell in ill and took his treatment under Dr. Tanbir Ahmed, MBBS (BCS Health) of Sarupkathi (Nesarabad Health Complex) and sent medical certificate by registered post on 15-5-2017 and 18-6-2017. After a long period 1st party came to the 2nd party-petitioner mill with a fitness certificate for joining his service but 2nd party prevented 1st party to join in the service and issued office Memo No. 24,04.4745,948.03.014.17.76/2124 dated 10-7-2017 dismissing the 1st party from his service, The 1st party finding no other alternatives has filed Srama Case Na 68 of 2017 before the Chairman, Divisional Labour Court, Khulna with prayer for declaration and direction as stated above. 

 3. The petitioner, as opposite party, contested the case denying all the material allegations brought by the 1st party-respondent No, 3. The 2nd party stated in the written statements that the case of the 1st party is not maintainable in its present form and also barred by limitation. Service record of 1st party is not satisfactory. The 1st party was rightly and lawfully dismissed from his service after complying all the legal formalities giving sufficient opportunity to defend himself. The 1st party was appointed by the opposite party-petitioner on 1-4-1995 as helper on ad-hoc basis and subsequently, he became permanent on 1-4-1995 His last post and designation was Helper, Mota tat Division, shift 'Ka' Mill No.1 2nd party never got satisfied by the work of 1st party After joining his service the 1st party on several times found absent from office without any leave. Due to such unauthorized absent for a long period, the departmental head sent inter Divisional letter on 6-6-2000, Bureau of Labour issued show cause Notice on 11-6-2000 and caution letter No. 131/203. Mill authority further issued caution letter being No. 1370/2000 dated 9-9-2000 and 25-3-2006 due to unauthorized absence and further issued final caution letter and complain on 16-3-2013. On 26-5-2016 the authority issued show cause notice due to absence of 15 days asking to reply within 10 days, but the 1st party did not join in service or replied the show cause notice. Thereafter, mill authority issued caution letter on 31-5-2016 and show cause notice on 31-5-2017 but no reply was made by the 1st party Finding no other alternatives, the 2nd party issued dismissal order being No. 24,04.4745,948.03.014.17.76/2124 dated 10-7-2017. 

 8. He further submits that the respondent Na 3 in the past also acted in the same manner when he went on leave for which he was warned once again not to repeat the same, but the respondent No. 3 did not change his habit of absenting from his duty without leave. Therefore, the petitioner had no other alternative but to dismiss the respondent No. 3 from service, accordingly, the petitioner dismissed him. It is also argued that the petitioner company closed its business on and from 30-6-2013, as such, the petitioner has no stop to reinstate the respondent No. 3 in the service, but the Labour Court as well as the Labour Appellate Court while allowing the case of the respondent Na 3 and dismissing the appeal most unfortunately failed to appreciate the fact of the case as well as evidences both oral and documentary placed before the court at the time of hearing. 

 9. Mrs Zubaida Gulshan Ara, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent No. 3 submits that admittedly, the respondent Na. 3 went on leave from 6-5-2017 to 15-5-2017 for 10 days and when he was on leave he fell in ill with various deceases, consequently, he was taking treatment and the fact of his illness was duly communicated and informed to the petitioner company with medical certificate twice which was received by the company in time After recovery, the respondent No. 3 went to join the service, but the company did not allow him to join, rather by letter dated 10-7-017 dismissed the respondent No, 3 from service, challenging which the respondent No. 3 filed. Labour Case No. 68 of 2017 before the Labour Court, 'Chu1na, which was allowed by judgment and order dated 4-12-2018 and found that the respondent No. 3 was dismissed illegally without drawing any proceeding under sections 23,24 and 27 of the Labour Ain, 2016 as amended. Against the judgment and order of the Labour Court, present petitioner preferred Appeal No. 03 of 2019 before the Labour Appellate Tribunal, Dhaka which was also dismissed by the judgment and order dated 13-8-2020, wherein, the appellate court also found that the respondent No, 3 was dismissed by the company without following any procedure provided in Labour Ain, 2006. 

 12. Admittedly, the respondent No. 3 was appointed in the petitioner company on 1-4 1995. Since then he had been serving the company and he went on leave for 10 days starting from 6-5-2017 to 15-5-2017 As alleged by the respondent No. 3 that during his leave he suffered from diabetes and high blood pressure and had been suffering from high fever with vomiting. Consequently, he took treatment from the Doctor at Upazilla Health Complex, Sarupkathi and by a letter dated 21-5- 2017 enclosing medical certificate dated 15-5- 2017 informed and communicated the company about his illness. Because of further deterioration of his health he again took treatment and by a medical certificate dated 16- 6-1973 sent another representation to the company by post on 18-6-2017, After his recovery he went to join the service with medical certificate on 11-7-2017, but he was not allowed to join and handed over a letter dated 10-7-2017 saying that he has been dismissed from service. Thereafter, the respondent No. 3 served a grievance notice upon the company on 11-2-2017 urging upon the company to withdraw the dismissal letter as the same was issued illegally and without compliance of provisions of law and to allow him to join in the service but in vain, consequently, he filed Labour Case No. 68 of 2017 before the Labour Court. 

 13. The petitioner-company contended that the respondent No. 3 is of the habit of absenting from ditty without leave and in support of such contention submitted some documents showing that for the same offence the respondent No. 3 was earlier on several occasions warned and cautioned not to repeat the same in future, but he did not pay any heed to the warning and as usual absenting from service for long time. Consequently, the company by letter dated 20-5-2017 asked the respondent No. 3 to join in the service within 10 days and to explain why he remained absent without leave, but he did not reply the same and after long time on 11-7-2017 he came to join the service but before that date the company by letter dated 10-7-2017 dismissed him from service for unauthorized absence from services as such, his dismissal is legal and valid and there is no scope for reinstatement of the respondent No. 3 in the service. The Labour Court at the time of hearing of the case observed that misconduct of a worker and punishment has been described in section 23 and procedure to be followed against the delinquent under section 24 and in the event of long absence without leave the company must serve a notice giving 10 days to join in service and explain the fact and thereafter, further seven days show cause to be given to the delinquent and after receipt of the reply the company can release or discharge a worker from service under section 27(31(a) of the Labour Ain, but in the instant case though charge has been brought against the respondent No. 3 under section 23, but no punishment imposed by the company under said section and no proceeding was drawn up against the respondent No. 3 under section 24 of the Ain, but the action whatever taken by the company is under section 27(31(a) of the Labour Ain which provide as follows: 

 14. From plain reading of the section quoted above, it appears that under the said provision of law no dismissal of a worker warrants, but in the event of unauthorized absence and service of notice for 10 days and further 7 days if no reply is given by the delinquent the worker shall be deemed to have resigned from service and the company shall pay the worker benefits under section 27(4) of the Ain, but the petitioner dismissed him from service in violation of the provisions of section 27 (3ka). Taking the aforesaid provision of law and the facts of the present case in its entirety, the Labour Court as well as the Labour Appellate Court concurrently found that the respondent No. 3 was dismissed from service without following the provisions of law under sections 23, 24 and 27 of the Labour Ain and found that the dismissal is palpably illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 15. It is to be noted that in the event of finding the worker liable to be dismissed from service for misconduct, the company must proceed with that worker under section 24 of the Ain, by initiating a disciplinary proceeding or the provision of section 27(31(a) discharging the worker for unauthorized absence, but the company failed to lake recourse against the worker under any provisions of law. As such, we do not find any illegality or error in the judgment and order of both the courts below calling for interference by this Court.
